chapter.li: LEChapter13 Verse1 And it came to pass, the same day, Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seaside. VerseEnd Verse2 And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that he went into a ship and sat, and the whole multitude stood on the shore. VerseEnd Verse3 And he spoke many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow. VerseEnd Verse4 And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the wayside, and the fowls came and devoured them up. VerseEnd Verse5 Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth, and immediately they sprung up. VerseEnd Verse6 And when the sun was up, they were scorched because they had no deepness of earth; and because they had no root, they withered away. VerseEnd Verse7 And some fell among thorns, and the thorns sprung up and choked them. VerseEnd Verse8 But others fell into good ground and brought forth fruit: some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, and some thirtyfold. VerseEnd Verse9 Who has ears to hear, let him hear. VerseEnd

Verse10 Then the disciples came and said unto him, Why do you speak unto them in parables? VerseEnd Verse11 He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of Heaven, but to them it is not given; VerseEnd Verse12 for whoever receives, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance. But whoever continues not to receive, from him shall be taken away even that he has. VerseEnd Verse13 Therefore, I speak to them in parables because they seeing, see not, and hearing, they hear not, neither do they understand. VerseEnd Verse14 And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah concerning them, which says, By hearing you shall hear and shall not understand, and seeing you shall see and shall not perceive; VerseEnd Verse15 for this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed, lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their hearts, and should be converted, and I should heal them. VerseEnd

Verse16 But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear. VerseEnd Verse17 And blessed are you because these things have come unto you that you might understand them. And truly I say unto you, many righteous prophets have desired to see these days which you see, and have not seen them, and to hear that which you hear, and have not heard. VerseEnd

Verse18 Hear therefore the parable of the sower. VerseEnd Verse19 When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and understands not, then comes the wicked one and catches away that which was sown in his heart; this is he who received seed by the wayside. VerseEnd Verse20 But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that hears the word and readily with joy receives it, VerseEnd Verse21 yet he has not root in himself and endures but for a while; for when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he is offended. VerseEnd Verse22 He also who received seed among the thorns is he that hears the word, and the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful. VerseEnd Verse23 But he who received seed into the good ground is he that hears the word and understands and endures, which also bears fruit and brings forth: some a hundredfold, some sixty, and some thirty. VerseEnd

Verse24 Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of Heaven is likened unto a man who sowed good seed in his field, VerseEnd Verse25 but while he slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went his way. VerseEnd Verse26 But when the blade was sprung up and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. VerseEnd Verse27 So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, did not you sow good seed in your field? From where then does it have tares? VerseEnd Verse28 He said unto them, An enemy has done this. And the servants said unto him, Do you desire then that we go and gather them up? VerseEnd Verse29 But he said, Nay, lest while you gather up the tares, you root up also the wheat with them. VerseEnd Verse30 Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather together first the wheat into my barns, and the tares are bound in bundles to be burned. VerseEnd

Verse31 Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of Heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed which a man took and sowed in his field, VerseEnd Verse32 which indeed is the least of all seeds, but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. VerseEnd
Verse33 Another parable spoke he unto them: The kingdom of Heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened. VerseEnd

Verse34 All these things spoke Jesus unto the multitudes in parables, and without a parable spoke he not unto them, VerseEnd Verse35 that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world. VerseEnd

Verse36 Then Jesus sent the multitude away and went into the house. And his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field. VerseEnd Verse37 He answered and said unto them, He that sows the good seed is the Son of Man. VerseEnd Verse38 The field is the world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom, but the tares are the children of the wicked. VerseEnd Verse39 The enemy that sowed them is the Devil. The harvest is the end of the world, or the destruction of the wicked, and the reapers are the angels or the messengers sent of Heaven. VerseEnd Verse40 As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so shall it be in the end of this world, VerseEnd Verse41 or the destruction of the wicked. For in that day, before the Son of Man shall come, he shall send forth his angels and messengers of Heaven, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend and them who do iniquity, VerseEnd Verse42 and shall cast them out among the wicked. And there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth, for the world shall be burned with fire. VerseEnd Verse43 Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who has ears to hear, let him hear. VerseEnd

Verse44 Again, the kingdom of Heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in a field. And when a man has found a treasure which is hidden, he secures it, and immediately, for joy thereof, goes and sells all that he has and buys that field. VerseEnd

Verse45 Again, the kingdom of Heaven is like unto a merchant man seeking goodly pearls, VerseEnd Verse46 who, when he had found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had and bought it. VerseEnd

Verse47 Again, the kingdom of Heaven is like unto a net that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind, VerseEnd Verse48 which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away. VerseEnd Verse49 So shall it be at the end of the world — and the world is the children of the wicked. The angels shall come forth and sever the wicked from among the just VerseEnd Verse50 and shall cast them out into the world to be burned. There shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. VerseEnd

Verse51 Jesus said unto them, Have you understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord. VerseEnd Verse52 Then he said unto them, Every scribe well-instructed in the things of the kingdom of Heaven is like unto a householder, a man therefore who brings forth out of his treasure that which is new and old. VerseEnd

Verse53 And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there. VerseEnd Verse54 And when he had come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished and said, From where does this Jesus have this wisdom and these mighty works? VerseEnd Verse55 Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary? And his brethren, James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas, VerseEnd Verse56 and his sisters, are they not all with us? From where then does this man have all these things? VerseEnd Verse57 And they were offended at him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country and in his own house. VerseEnd Verse58 And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief. VerseEnd
